name: PA-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 23 points on the partisan index
Joyce holds a massive financial edge: $3.8 million on hand versus about $16,000 for Farnham
Incumbent Joyce is running again with no expert raters flagging the seat as competitive
Prediction markets price Democratic victory at only about 3 percent
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a deeply Republican district, a well-funded incumbent, a challenger with minimal resources, and markets showing almost no Democratic chance. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the race sits firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: Any surprise polling or major outside spending on Farnham's behalf would be needed to move this race, and nothing of the sort is evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 13th District, anchored in south-central Pennsylvania, is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, favoring Republicans by roughly 23 points on the partisan index. Republican John Joyce, first elected in 2018, is seeking another term with the full advantages of incumbency.

The financial picture is starkly one-sided: Joyce has raised about $2.4 million and holds $3.8 million on hand, while Democrat Beth Farnham has raised roughly $55,000 with about $16,000 available, and no outside groups have invested in the race. No public general-election polling exists and no expert raters list the seat as contested. Prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset, consistent with the district's fundamentals and the expectation of a comfortable Joyce victory.
